channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: DC shooting leaves 1 person killed, 4 injured. Gunman dead
item.description: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police. (Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history

item.title: How FRANCE 24 traced Tehran-backed Afghan fighters from Syria to southeastern Iran
item.description: Members of the Tehran-backed Afghan Shia militia known as the Fatemiyoun division have resurfaced in Iran after largely disappearing from public view following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria in 2024. FRANCE 24 used "martyrdom” announcements and the geolocation of videos shared on social media to trace their presence.

item.title: At least five people shot in DC neighbourhood near the White House
item.description: At least one person died after five people were shot early Thursday in a Washington, DC neighbourhood near the White House, police said. A swarm of officers responded to a nearby apartment building where a suspect was barricaded and later shot himself.

item.title: 1 dead, 4 injured in DC, as police respond to active shooting: Sources
item.description: The Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, D.C. are responding to an active shooter, police said Thursday.

item.title: Life through a lens: Celebrating 200 years of photography
item.description: A passport photo, a selfie, an award-winning film and even the evening news: all of them were made possible thanks to a "fantastic machine", the camera. As France celebrates the bicentenary of the first fixed photographic image, we discuss the image-obsessed society we live in with filmmaker Maximilien Van Aertryck and artist Alina Frieske.

item.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded at war memorial
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, along with his wife and aides, was silenced by a guard on Wednesday at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth's group was at Arlington National Cemetery for a Veterans Day ceremony when they were reprimanded for laughing and taking pictures in front of the sombre memorial.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations on extramarital affairs
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Washington Fraser Jackson and FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert have more.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its leather-jacket-clad leader at a crucial time for the sector.

item.title: European security and Ukraine talks top agenda at Dublin summit
item.description: Leaders from more than 50 European countries and institutions are gathering in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, hosted by Ireland under the theme “Europe – strong, secure and connected”. The summit highlighted the need for Europe to have a seat at the table in any discussions shaping its future, amid an ongoing debate over how the continent should respond to US-led efforts to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine with Russia. FRANCE 24's Europe Editor Armen Georgian tells us more.

item.title: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff went to the Kremlin to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin and are scheduled to fly later to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. (Image credit: Vyacheslav Prokofyev)

item.title: Australia: Teen found alive after six days missing in bush
item.description: A 17-year-old Australian has been found alive and well after spending six days missing in bushland east of Melbourne. After being spotted by helicopter, the teen was winched to safety before an emotional reunion with his mother who joked that “he’s never leaving the house again”.

item.title: For the love of French butter: 'Le beurre' spreading joy globally
item.description: French butter is having a moment! We dive into France's love of butter, the many rules that apply to "le beurre", how tourists are hauling back flavoured artisan butter as souvenirs, and how the French language has embraced many a butter expression over the years.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid alleged affair with suspected spy
item.description: CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim chief executive, Nvidia said.

item.title: Armed robbers flee Paris De Beers store on motorcycles after jewellery heist
item.description: Four black-clad individuals sped away from De Beers jeweller in Paris's second arrondissement Thursday morning after stealing hundreds of thousands of euros worth of luxury goods at gunpoint. Police are searching for those responsible.

item.title: Democrat Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom will win the election for U.S. Senate in Mississippi, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: ICRC 'currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed.

item.title: France's social safety net: Can it afford to be so generous?
item.description: Created in the aftermath of World War II, France's social security system has become one of the pillars of French society, providing everything from healthcare and family benefits to pensions. But with an ageing population and mounting deficits, this ambitious model is facing a major financial test. We look at how the system works, why it is so deeply valued by the French and whether the country can afford to keep its promise of protecting everyone – from cradle to grave.

item.title: Mississippi elects its first African American to US Senate since Reconstruction
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black US Senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory, confirmed on November 11 after prolonged ballot counting, marks a major political shift in the conservative state. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
item.description: Raka is the son of former President Joko Widodo. The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements. (Image credit: Tatan Syuflana)

item.title: France: Five men on trial for murder of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci's brother
item.description: In France, the trial of five men accused of murdering the brother of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci is under way. Amine Kessaci, originally known as an environmental activist, became a prominent figure in the fight against drug-related crime after losing two of his brothers to violence linked to drug trafficking. The defendants face the possibility of life imprisonment. The verdict is expected on Monday, November 16. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley tells us more.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal
item.description: Huang co-founded the chipmaker Nvidia, which has become one of the driving forces behind the AI boom. But reports that he may have had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy quickly sank his career. (Image credit: Sean Gallup)

item.title: Huang powers and bankrolls AI revolution: Nvidia CEO caught between 'a rock and a very hard place'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of France's Institute of Digital Sovereignty. Benhamou examines the intersection of traditional espionage, geopolitical rivalry and the extraordinary concentration of power within the global AI industry. Discussing allegations surrounding Nvidia's leadership, he describes the chipmaker as "the banker of the global AI system," a striking characterization that captures the company's importance not merely as a semiconductor manufacturer, but as a central actor in the economic and technological infrastructure underpinning the AI boom. "Because humans stay humans." Benhamou identifies one of the central paradoxes of the artificial intelligence revolution: even as technological systems acquire unprecedented strategic and economic importance, the individuals who control them remain susceptible to familiar forms of influence, manipulation and misjudgment.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair raises national security concerns
item.description: Nvidia announced on Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang was stepping down following revelations that he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The company's chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for Huang's successor.

item.title: Can the fight against climate change be good for business?
item.description: Industries across the globe are seeking to reduce their carbon footprint and become more sustainable. To do so, many are turning to employees with specific credentials. According to LinkedIn's Global Green Skills Report 2026, workers with green skills are being hired at more than 1.5 times the rate of the wider workforce.

item.title: US jobless claims tick up to 200,000 but remain low by historic standards
item.description: More Americans applied for unemployed benefits last week, but jobless claims remain at historically low levels, layoffs are rare and most workers enjoy unusual job security

item.title: Midterms: Democrat Colom claims historic win in Mississippi
item.description: Scott Colom has become the first Black person to win a Senate race in Mississippi since 1874 and the first Democrat to do so since 1982 after being declared the victor in a razor-edge election on Wednesday. The win is a stunning upset in one of the country’s most reliably red states, adding to what were already sweeping gains by the Democrats at the midterms.

item.title: Iran live updates: 'We don't need a deal with Iran,' Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: War photographer Patrick Chauvel: 'People have lost faith in the press'
item.description: One of France's top war photographers, who has a 50-year CV of taking pictures in and around conflicts across the planet, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his concerns that people have lost faith in the press. He notes that journalists are only looking for the truth. Patrick Chauvel has produced nearly 380,000 photographs, from Vietnam to Cambodia, from Afghanistan to Palestine, from Lebanon to Ukraine. He says he wants to take people by the hand to show them how the press works and why.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
item.description: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.

item.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
item.description: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.

item.title: WATCH: Historic ocean liner sunk to become artificial reef
item.description: The historic SS United States, once the fastest ship on the seas, made a slow final journey beneath the waters Wednesday.

item.title: Two Iranians convicted of spying for their country after entering Britain illegally
item.description: Two Iranian nationals who arrived in the UK illegally have been found guilty of spying for their country in the first case of its kind.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, health ministry says
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.title: Anti-migrant activist admits slashing boat with a knife in English Channel
item.description: An anti-immigration activist has pleaded guilty to criminal damage after using a knife to slash a migrant boat in the English Channel.

item.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now. (Image credit: Jake Crandall)

item.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
item.description: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

item.title: Trump proposed a 'secret weapon' to police colleges. It will soon become reality
item.description: In a 2023 campaign speech, Trump pledged to reclaim universities from what he called the radical left. His Education Department just finalized a rule to help him do it.

item.title: Kennedy Center plans Ticketmaster switch, raising conflict of interest concerns
item.description: The Kennedy Center's former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the same time the two parties were negotiating. (Image credit: Shannon Finney)

item.title: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from DA to Mississippi's Democratic U.S. Senator
item.description: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black Senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics. (Image credit: Rogelio V. Solis)

item.title: Bomb alert at Calais train station disrupts Eurostar
item.description: A bomb alert at a French train station disrupted journeys including international travel, with Eurostar trains among those affected.

item.title: Poundland secures extended deadline for possible rescue
item.description: Crisis-hit Poundland has secured an extended deadline for a potential rescue amid political pressure for a solvent sale of the chain.

item.title: WATCH: Scott Colom delivers acceptance speech in Jackson, Mississippi
item.description: Senator-elect Scott Colom is Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction in the 1870s.

item.title: WATCH: How Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom's win is 145 years in the making
item.description: ABC News' Faith Abuby details the historic win of Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom as the state's first Democrat to win a Senate seat since 1982 and the first Black senator since Reconstruction.

item.title: Fiery clashes erupt in Spain as millions join general strike
item.description: Unrest broke out in cities across Spain on Wednesday after millions of workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years.

item.title: Several Democrats missed the crucial Hegseth impeachment vote. Many blamed traffic
item.description: Eleven Dems missed the critical vote, squandering Hegseth's impeachment attempt.

item.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed

item.title: Trump administration moves to drop millions from SNAP food assistance
item.description: An analysis by USDA estimates that over 6 million people could lose benefits.

item.title: WATCH: President Trump pays tribute to veterans
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.title: Pope ends Argentina visit with unity plea after pushing back against Milei's agenda
item.description: Pope Leo closed an emotional visit to Argentina with an appeal for unity and reconciliation, offering a message of hope to his predecessor's polarised homeland.

item.title: Top WH lawyer warns Democrats that threats of oversight could be criminally probed
item.description: The warning came in a Monday letter from White House counsel Will Scharf.

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: WATCH: Blockbuster NFL trades
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer has details on the big trades, including Kirk Cousins heading to the Minnesota Vikings.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.title: WATCH: NYC tour helicopter makes hard landing in New Jersey
item.description: The pilot of a New York City sightseeing helicopter is being praised for pulling off a remarkable emergency landing in Bayonne, New Jersey, after the chopper’s tail rotor broke off.

item.title: WATCH: These NFL cheerleaders balance life in the military
item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.

item.title: Four grizzly bears killed mother and daughter in Canada
item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.title: WATCH: What first responders want you to know about surviving rising waters
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.title: WATCH: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
item.description: Five months after Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty, he celebrated a moment that once seemed far from certain: marrying his fiancee, Haley.

item.title: WATCH: Woman living the 'dream' to save foxes in need
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman who's on a mission to save foxes at a sanctuary in upstate New York.

item.title: Two Premier League managers sacked in a matter of hours
item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has been sacked.
